PHOTO: Vecteezy / MGN (AP) — Ukraine launched hundreds of drones across Russia on Sunday, killing at least six people in one of Kyiv’s largest aerial attacks of the war. Kyiv has stepped up its attacks on Russia this year, with long-range missiles and swarms of drones targeting military industries and energy facilities. It has also increasingly pummeled giant Wildberries depots, burning billions of dollars’ worth of merchandise belonging to the Russian online retail giant. Those attacks have brought the war home to the Russian public nearly 4½ years into Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Meanwhile, Ukraine also came under Russian attack, with drone strikes destroying homes and torching Kyiv’s landmark book market. Russia’s Ministry of Defense said it had destroyed 822 Ukrainian drones overnight. Some 600 drones were detected headed toward the Russian capital, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said, with a third of those destroyed over the Moscow region itself. An 83-year-old man was killed after a Ukrainian drone hit a private home in the Moscow region, local Gov. Andrey Vorobyov said. He also confirmed that a Ukrainian attack had sparked a blaze at a Wildberries warehouse in the town of Podolsk. A drone attack targeted three towns in Russia’s southwestern Rostov region, killing five people, local Gov. Yury Slyusar said. The attack, with more than 150 drones, damaged several homes and a railway station and sparked a forest fire. Russian strikes kill 5 in Ukraine A Russian missile attack on Ukraine’s Kryvyi Rih killed two people and wounded 14 others, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote on social media Sunday. He also said that one more person had been killed in the city of Sumy. ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine’s largest steel producer, confirmed that one of its sites had been hit in a missile attack and that operations had been partially suspended. Elsewhere, a man and a woman died when their home was hit by a Russian strike in Ukraine’s southern Zaporizhzhia region, said Ivan Fedorov, the head of the local military administration. Russian attacks also sparked fires throughout the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, wounding six people. A blaze took hold at one of the city’s largest book markets, tearing through kiosks huddled close to the Pochaina metro station. Firefighters fought back the flames, which sent plumes of black smoke across the capital, and picked their way through rubble where the market’s crowded pavilions once stood. “Wherever the Russians can reach with their ballistic missiles, they strike civilian infrastructure,” Zelenskyy said. Russia’s Ministry of Defense said Sunday that it had targeted a metallurgical plant in Kryvyi Rih and several military-industrial sites in Kyiv, including a manufacturing facility for Ukraine’s Flamingo missiles. The domestically produced missiles are increasingly key to Ukraine’s long-range attacks on Russia, with Zelenskyy announcing Saturday that Kyiv had used the weapons to attack a rocket research and production center in Samara approximately 900 kilometers (560 miles) from the Ukrainian border. NATO jet downs drone in Romanian airspace Romania’s Ministry of National Defense said Sunday that a Spanish Air and Space Force F-18 fighter jet shot down a drone that had entered Romanian airspace. The drone’s entry into the NATO member’s airspace was detected by surveillance systems at 4:44 a.m., the ministry said, about 24 kilometers (14.9 miles) north of the eastern city of Galati near the border with neighboring Moldova. Moldova is a landlocked country between Ukraine and Romania. A Spanish F-18 aircraft that was performing air policing duties “made radar contact with the target and received engagement approval,” the ministry said. “The drone was safely shot down by the F-18 aircraft at 05:01.” The ministry later said that drone debris was also reported in the Black Sea around 10 a.m. on Sunday, about 1.5 kilometers (0.9 miles) from the coastal city of Constanta. Separately, another drone fragment was found on Sunday 1 nautical mile (1.85 kilometers) from Constanta. Romanian officials did not specify the drone’s origin. However, Moldova’s Ministry of Defense said Sunday that its Army surveillance systems had detected a Geran-type Shahed drone in Moldovannews airspace, which entered from Ukraine and exited toward Romania. The spate of drone incidents comes weeks after Romanian pilots shot down three drones over three days as Russia intensified attacks against Ukraine near the border. Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Romania has reported dozens of drone incidents, including some that have crashed and exploded on its territory. Acting Foreign Minister Oana Toiu said in a post on X that the Spanish deployment in Romania was scaled up “at the request of Romania and NATO to bolster the Eastern Flank following prior drone incidents,” and that it was Spain’s fourth such deployment. By Oliver Boyd-Barrett Icons of Bad Faith and Incompetence OLIVER BOYD-BARRETT SEP 05, 2026 Kushner and Witkoff: "They are great negotiators".— Donald Trump T iming may be all important today, and this posting can be no more than a draft. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner landed in Moscow earlier today, September 5th, with a reported aim of reviving negotiations over Ukraine. The envoys were met at the airport on Saturday by the Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev, a businessman best known for his participation in talks on potential US-Russian economic and business opportunities (none of which, so far as I am aware, have made headway). According to the Guardian, Trump yesterday claimed that he had a new proposal to end the war, without providing any details on what his new plan might be. The tempation to yawn is all but irresistible, but you never know. There are conflicting accounts as to whether both sides have declared a pause in their airstrikes. For Military Summary Channel earlier today the situation was that Zelenskiy had unilaterally declared a ceasefire along front lines while reserving the right to respond to Russian “violations” of a ceasefire to which it has not agreed. It is not clear - to me, at any rate, even if we accept this is accurate - whether this is separate from Zelenskiy’s declaration that he would stop its airstrikes on Moscow during the visit of Kushner and Witkoff. According to the Guardian, the Kremlin spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, said on Saturday that Putin had ordered a 72-hour pause in its strikes on Kyiv, given that Kushner and Witkoff are expected to proceed to visit Kiev on Sunday after they have met with Russian President Putin today. Overnight there was a major Russian drone and missile attack across Ukraine. Zelenskoy accused Russia of trying to disrupt the envoys’ visit to Ukraine with strikes on Kyiv’s two airports overnight. Officials visiting Ukraine have largely done so by train, as Ukrainian airspace has been closed since 2022 due to the war. Zelenskiy has this week attempted to persuade commercial airlines not to fly in Russian airspace on the grounds that Ukrainian drones are making Russian airports and airspace unsafe. Zelenskiy has also pleaded with the UN to close Russian airspace. More precisely, on September 1, 2026, Zelenskyy stated that Russian airspace would be “de facto closed” and unsafe for civilian carriers as Ukraine ramps up its drone strikes on Russian logistics and military infrastructure. While Western commercial airlines stopped flying over Russia after the 2022 invasion, carriers from countries like China, Turkey, and various Gulf states still use Russian skies. Some foreign airlines have begun suspending flights following the warning. Ukraine formally notified the UN and its civil aviation agency, the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), regarding the risks to civilian aviation. Zelenskiy emphasized that Ukraine does not target civilian aircraft (mmm - MH17?) but noted that the sheer scale of upcoming drone activity means air traffic must account for the danger. Russian President Vladimir Putin strongly condemned the announcement, labeling it a “declaration of state terrorism” and an unlawful interference with civil aviation, while filing a formal protest with the ICAO. One option that Russia has by way of retaliating against Ukrainian efforts to shut its airspace is to continue bombardment of Kiev’s major railway station and network, the usual port of entry for visiting Western diplomats, politicians, military advisers and the like, a process that is apparently already under way. It is too early to say anything assertive about the Kushner and Witkoff visit and its likelihood of “success.” Almost certainly the visit, like CIA director Ratcliffe’s visit a week ago, and like the US pressure on Putin’s “allies” within the SCO/BRICS (notably India, Turkiye and Brazil) is intended to push Putin into somehow ending the war. It is inconceivable to me that the US can come up with terms that would be acceptable to Russia, to Ukraine, to Europe and to the US neocon-dominated Congress. In my view, Russia is already making a mistake in allowing Witkoff and Kushner into the country. Indeed, I find Putin’s ability to flatter the two “envoys” nauseous. Putin has showered praise on Witkoff and Kushner, describing them as “sincere people” who are trying to give “concrete substance” to the negotiation process. He stated that they are “always welcome guests” in Moscow and noted that Russia finds it highly “convenient to work with them”. Putin highlighted that because U.S. President Donald Trump deeply trusts these two envoys, it gives their interactions true meaning. He noted that agreements would be useless if the top official disregarded their input. Such sentiments, in my view, are unacceptable in application to two men who have no elected legitimacy other than Trump likes them; are not professional diplomats; whose interests seemingly align more with business aspirations than geopolitical agreements; who are known to have contributed to the weaponization of diplomacy with a view to inducing Washington’s opponents to lower their guard in advance of unprovoked and murderous attacks by Washington and Israel. They are icons of malignancy, bad faith, and incompetence. And they are committed Zionists. I do not find Putin’s tolerance for these ghouls remotely amusing or clever or “diplomatic.” It is, instead, an insult to Russian honor, to the honor of those whom Kushner and Witkoff have previously betrayed - as in the case of Iran - and to the honor of the Global South in general. Most important of all, it is because of them and because of the actions of their master, Trump, that the US has become agreement incapable and is recognized throughout much of the world as being so. In short, there is no agreement possible with these gentlemen that could be worth its salt and in which there can be any sane reason for investing trust and hope. I understand that Putin thinks he needs to meet with them so as to show his critics within the SCO/BRICS, and to show the people of Ukraine and Europe, that he has done his best to seek a reasonable agreement, no matter how unreasonable and untrustworthy his interlocutors are. He can do that without odious flattery, although I think he is better off not doing it at all. Right-winger Modi continues with his treacherous flim-flam. He has got no reason to respect or to put on a performance for Zelenskiy, who lacks all legitimacy and whose ouster (by neo-Nazi Azov regiment leader Andriy Biletsky?) will be universally unlamented. Nor for India’s Modi, whose pious waffling represents a tired and shameful refusal to commit whole-heartedly to the goals of multipolarity in resistance to US bullying. Nor for Brazil’s Lula, whose status as a pro-democracy man of the people is now stripped naked by the dismal scandal of the power of corrupt Supreme Court justice Alexandre de Moraes and pay-offs from disgraced banker Daniel Vorcaro, a scandal that will quite likely shoe the son of jailed former leader Bolsonaro into power and complete the delivery of almost all of Latin America into the hands of a Zionist-loving clique of rightwing oligarchs, and perhaps spell the end of the BRICS as anything more than a convenient forum for non-dollar trading alliances, devoid of any genuine political or moral vision for the world. I don’t think it likely that Kushner and Witkoff will walk away with anything resembling a diplomatic coup; a nothing-burger is more plausible. Russia is winning on the battlefields and Ukrainian defenses are crumbling - as in Odessa and along what remains of Ukraine’s Black Sea coast, in the Slavyansk-Kramatorsk conurbation in Donbass, in Orekihiv in Zapporizhzhia and soon in the city of Zapporizhzhia itself, in northeast Kharkiv and around the city of Kharkiv, in northern Chernihiv and Sumy and their eponymous capitals so close to Kiev. There are increasing signs of panic in Kiev, represented by the shoot-out this week in public in Kiev between the nation’s two foremost intelligence agencies and by Zelenskiy’s irritable blaming of Europeans for not providing him more money and more interceptors, indications that Kiev is sorely lacking in the funding necessary for its survival beyond the end of this year and confirmation of the dwindling availability of air defenses and other weaponry, and the declining volume and efficacy of Ukrainian drone and missile attacks on Russia. My own expectations at this point are that Russia will continue with this struggle until it has taken control over the entirety of Ukraine east of the Dnieper together with the Odessa oblast and the remainder of Ukraine’s Black Sea coast. It will leave behind a rump state, based in Kiev (unless Russia decides to take that, too, and it might well) or in Lvov in the far west that, under the terms of an unconditional surrender that Russia will impose, will subscribe to all of Russia’s key demands including that of Ukrainian neutrality. That rump state may or may not seek territorial alignments with Poland and Romania and Hungary, although I am now downgrading the plausibility of such a development as it would occasion possibly fatal ripple effects across the entirety of the European Union. The neo-Nazi forces represented by Zelenskiy, who may well have been a western agent from the beginning, will likely receive European support in setting up a government-in-exile somewhere pleasant in Europe, perhaps Paris and which will be the go-to entity if Germany is successful in leading the rest of Europe into a wholescale war with Russia and needs a plausible new regime in power in Ukraine. While we can expect Germany to be persistent in this ambition and to find many allies across Europe, I do not think that it will actually be successful in such an endeavor. Here are my main reasons: (1) Following the demise of Trump and MAGA irrationality, even under a Democratic government still deeply corrupted by lunatic neocons from within, the US will begin to reacquire a thirst for rationality, morality, freedom from the bonds of imperial overreach, and content with a more moderate, realistic status as a collective of a mere 349 million on a planet that hosts 8.3 billion human beings. It will want nothing to do with the emergence of a European neofascist hate fest against Russia that pits one system of moderate capitalism against another and serves the best interests, ultimately, of the US system of extreme capitalism. In short, a European assault on Russia will have to do without the US, and if Europe is too successful (improbable), then the US may feel moved to enter (or threaten to enter) the war on Russia’s side as it cannot defeat Russia and China combined. (2) Germany faces a long, uphill climb to begin to mobilize forces that are sufficient to pose an obstacle to Russia and that will allow themselves to be so mobilized, or to re-arm to the extent that would be necessary, given that Russian weapons production capacity well exceeds that of Germany and of NATO generally, is expanding every year, and will have the additional support, hardly trivial, of China, North Korea and Iran. Not only is Germany actually de-industrializing but, like virtually all of its fellow members within NATO, it is saddling itself with runaway debt costs that may very well finish off the collective West long before the opening salvos of a a suicidal war of global annihilation. Besides, there are also gathering forces of resistance within Germany (AfD) and France (Marine le Pen) and Italy (League) - the UK, to its shame, not so much - that may yet stop the warmongers in their tracks. However, there is no room for complacency. The conflict will not disappear. It will likely linger for decades in the form of guerrilla warfare and low intensity conflict, a constant headache both for NATO and for Russia, whose final end point is difficult to predict. https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/01/un-d.text: United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk has called for an urgent investigation into the death of a UN staff member in Houthi custody.Mohammad el Shami, who worked at the UN Human Rights Office in Yemen, died after being "arbitrarily held" by the Houthis since 6 June 2024, according to a statement from the high commissioner's office on Saturday.Shami's family said he had died more than a month ago but that they had only recently been informed, per the statement.Türk called his death a "heartbreaking loss" for the UN as he expressed his condolences to Shami's family and loved ones.He added that the family had not received "any explanation of the cause or circumstances of his death" and demanded transparency from Houthi authorities."This requires disclosure of all relevant medical and detention records, preservation of evidence and independent scrutiny of any stated cause of death. There must be accountability for wrongdoing," Türk said.“I am also gravely concerned for the safety and wellbeing of the other UN personnel who remain detained, including seven colleagues from my Office, as well as detained humanitarian and civil society workers. I appeal again for their immediate and unconditional release," he added.Yemeni Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani condemned the death and said the Houthis "bear full responsibility."He added that more than 70 UN staff members and dozens of humanitarian workers remain in Houthi custody.In June 2024, the Houthis said a number of people they accused of belonging to a US-Israeli "spy network" had been arrested in Yemen.The Iran-aligned Houthi rebels have launched a renewed offensive in Yemen in recent months, seizing territory as fighting with the country's internationally recognised government has intensified.Neighbouring Saudi Arabia has carried out strikes against the group in a bid to hamper its advance, prompting the Houthis to launch missiles and drones at Saudi cities and shipping. The group also declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia in July.A Houthi strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International airport last month left 13 people dead and more than 300 injured, according to Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation.
